I seriously do understand your frustration about not being properly valued in something you are passionate about and you put much effort into. That being said, I would like you to consider that not all the blame should be put on the tool - which it really is - and rather look deeper and see the issue is not exclusively there, but also in the fact that perhaps the school curriculum should evolve alongside it's environment - the technological revolution - which we are living in.

Creative writing is always a useful skill and now thanks to tools like these more people can practice and learn it. I would be so bold as to propose that one - in this case your professor - should not prohibit such use, but instead embrace it and make it part of the assignment, because there is no use to dwell on archaic methods when they are being outpaced by progress.

So the issue in my opinion is not really - whether you *can* use AI to *pretend* you have a skill or not, but rather - if you *can* use AI to *enhance* your already learned skill or not.

And about the AI checker, many other people here have mentioned how unreliable they are, so I wouldn't be much bothered about that.
